title: Design like Karpathy is watching — Zeke Sikelianos, Replicate
talk_summary: Zeke Sikelianos recounts how Karpathy's MenuGen blog post exposed Replicate's developer-experience failures, and argues that the primary consumer of docs and APIs is now an LLM, not a human. He prescribes llms.txt markdown docs, curl-first examples, OpenAPI schemas turned into MCP servers, boring technology, and slim information-dense JSON responses.

takeaways.technique: OpenAPI schema as single source of truth, auto-exposed as MCP
takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain one well-written OpenAPI JSON schema that generates human docs, SDKs, and an MCP server, so any LLM client can drive the whole API after adding one JSON line and a token.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all we really had to do to make this possible was invest in having an open API schema that was very well written

takeaways.technique: llms.txt / markdown docs instead of HTML
takeaways.what_they_do: They collapse elaborate docs sites into a single markdown file with a copy button, plus per-page 'copy as markdown' and 'send to Claude/ChatGPT' actions, because that is the format models consume best.
takeaways.evidence_quote: tired elaborate docs pages with fancy color palettes, branding, animations ... one single docs markdown file and a copy to clipboard button

takeaways.what_they_do: They design JSON responses knowing they land in a context window, trimming payloads to what an LLM needs rather than dumping everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of dumping a JSON payload response that has everything about all the models under the sun, consider making it a more small, slim down, information dense version

takeaways.what_they_do: They lead with a single curl command that encodes method, payload, auth, sync/async, and endpoint, because that one line teaches a model the whole call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LLMs don't like to click, they like to curl

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue models write better code for long-established tech (e.g. SQL) because training data is dense, so tech choice should account for model familiarity.
They treat a feature as unfinished until documented in LLM-consumable form, making docs part of shipping rather than an afterthought.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's not done until it's documented and the world knows about it. And an LLM can consume the content
